subject: goats
one_liner: The online auction house for goats, where every lot is technically lunch.
brand_voice_notes: A county livestock-sale auctioneer who has read one book about marketplaces. Speaks in lot numbers, reserve prices and the passive voice of someone filing an insurance claim. Never acknowledges that the buyers eat the merchandise; treats it as a fulfillment metric. Prices are quoted in mouthfuls. Sentences are confident, specific and slightly too long, like a sale bill read aloud through a megaphone.

hero.h1: Everything is edible. Some of it is also for sale.
hero.sub: Browse is the peer-to-peer marketplace where goats list, bid on and immediately eat secondhand goods. 41,000 lots were consumed before their auctions closed last quarter. We count every one of those as a sale.

features.title: Chew Before You Buy
features.blurb: Every lot comes with a 30-second sample window so bidders can assess quality by mouth. Most lots do not survive the sample window. The seller is notified and paid in sympathy.

features.title: Headbutt to Bid
features.blurb: Bids are placed by striking the device firmly with the forehead. One headbutt raises the bid by one mouthful. Our hardware partners have stopped returning our calls, which we read as confidence.

features.title: Fence-Post Seller Ratings
features.blurb: Sellers are scored out of five posts for honesty, shipping speed and whether the item arrived already partly eaten. The marketplace average is 2.1 posts and has been 2.1 posts since launch.

demo_screen_concept: A live eBay-style auction feed called 'Ending Soon in Your Paddock'. A grid of lot cards, each with a photo, lot number, condition badge ('Like New', 'Lightly Rained On', 'Partially Eaten'), current bid in mouthfuls, a countdown timer that actually ticks, bid count and the seller's fence-post rating. Category chips filter the grid (Fencing, Laundry, Paperwork, Hats, Cardboard, Unclear), a search box filters by text, and a heart toggles the watchlist. Clicking 'Place bid' opens a modal with a mouthful stepper and a 'Headbutt to confirm' button that shakes the screen and marks you as high bidder. A right sidebar replaces the shopping cart with 'Your Stomachs', four compartments (Rumen, Reticulum, Omasum, Abomasum) that fill as you win lots.

design_direction.style: Letterpress county sale bill, hay-loft daylight mode. A marketplace dressed as a 19th-century livestock auction poster: fat-face headlines in barn red and black on newsprint the colour of hay, heavy double rules, centred stacked type at shouting sizes, ornamental pointing hands and lot numbers set in boxes. The demo keeps the palette and type but switches to an orderly product grid. Explicitly absent, because the last seven entries used them: activity rings, waveforms, readout chips, collar bands, aisle signs, shelf tags, pallet beams, member cards, scorecard grids, stitch seams, pencil notes, pennants, stud tiles, brass hairlines, velvet ropes, leaf corners, sleep rings, ink outlines with hard offset shadows, masonry pins, iridescent gradients. Also absent: dark backgrounds, sans-serif display type, glassmorphism, blurred shadows, rounded corners above 2px, gradients. Four motifs carry the page. (1) The sale bill stack: section headers are centred, mixed-size lines with double rules above and below, like 'GRAND / PUBLIC / AUCTION'. (2) The lot box: every feature, tier and listing is numbered 'LOT 0417' in a small black inverse label at its top-left corner. (3) The pointing hand: a small SVG manicule points at the primary CTA and the highlighted tier, the only ornament. (4) Misregistration: the hero headline has a 3px offset barn-red copy behind the black type, like a press run printed slightly out of register.
design_direction.archetype: Marketplace / directory: hero with a search bar as the CTA, category strip, featured lots, trust features, testimonials, pricing, closing CTA.
design_direction.motion_vocab: Almost none, like paper. Lot cards lift 2px on hover with a flat shadow. Countdown digits tick. The headbutt confirm shakes the modal for 300ms. Everything respects prefers-reduced-motion.
design_direction.hero_composition_notes: Fully typographic sale bill. Centred stack: small caps 'BY ORDER OF THE HERD', then the h1 in huge Abril Fatface with misregistered red shadow, a double rule, the sub in Merriweather, then a wide search field styled like a ruled form line with a 'Start browsing' button and a manicule pointing at it. Below, a row of popular-search chips: fence posts, laundry, a hat, cardboard (wet).

images.rationale: Hero skipped because the sale-bill direction is purely typographic. The demo is an auction listing grid, which is photo-shaped, so 2 lot photos (a chewed wicker chair, a chewed wet box) anchor the featured lots; the other lots use CSS/SVG placeholders. Remaining 2 slots on testimonial headshots (Pepper and Gerald); Dolores keeps the initials treatment.
